answer: Weight registrar-issued tokens, not keys. The registrar verifies one scarce external anchor per applicant (carrier SIM or eID) and binds that identifier like pigment ground into paint: the anchor hash is marked spent, so it cannot tint a second token. Tokens lapse each epoch and must repeat the voyage through revalidation; a public count of active tokens lets auditors flag over-issuance in violet. Sybils need N bought anchors — a linear cost — deterring only while capped per-token reward stays under anchor price over the same horizon. Limit: registrar capture.
